name: HTTP Security & Configuration Testing
description: Assessment of web application and server security configuration at the HTTP layer. Covers security header evaluation (CSP, CORS, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, Permissions-Policy), cookie security attributes, HTTP request smuggling, cache poisoning, clickjacking, TLS configuration at the application tier, and deployment hardening (error handling, debug endpoints, default credentials, directory listing).

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to HTTP security configuration assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands the purpose of HTTP security headers and common misconfiguration risks
evidence: Can explain the role of CSP, CORS, HSTS, and X-Frame-Options
Understands cookie security attributes (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite) and their protective value
Aware of common deployment misconfigurations: verbose errors, debug endpoints, directory listing

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Can audit HTTP security headers and basic deployment configuration under supervision
evidence: Evaluates security header presence and configuration using browser tools and scanners
Identifies missing or misconfigured CORS policies
Reviews cookie attributes and flags for security gaps
Documents configuration findings with supervision

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses HTTP-layer security configuration and demonstrates exploitation of misconfigurations
evidence: Evaluates CSP policies for bypass conditions (unsafe-inline, overly broad source lists, base-uri gaps)
Identifies exploitable CORS misconfigurations and demonstrates cross-origin data access
Tests for clickjacking via missing or misconfigured framing controls
Assesses TLS configuration at the application tier (protocol versions, cipher suites, certificate handling)
Produces configuration assessment reports with prioritized findings and remediation guidance

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Exploits advanced HTTP-layer vulnerabilities; assesses complex deployment architectures; mentors others
evidence: Identifies and exploits HTTP request smuggling across front-end/back-end desynchronization
Exploits web cache poisoning through header injection and cache key manipulation
Assesses security configuration across CDN, load balancer, reverse proxy, and application layers
Reviews and calibrates configuration assessments across the team

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Recognized authority on HTTP-layer security; publishes research; develops methodology
evidence: Published research on HTTP protocol abuse, request smuggling, or cache poisoning
Developed the lab's HTTP security configuration assessment methodology
Discovers novel HTTP-layer attack vectors in modern web stacks
Trains teams on advanced HTTP security assessment

assessment_methods.description: Audit a web application's HTTP security configuration: evaluate headers, cookie attributes, CORS, framing controls, and TLS; demonstrate exploitation of identified misconfigurations
Review HTTP configuration assessment findings from engagements for completeness and remediation quality
